Eligibility for a chemotherapy protocol following radical cystectomy is considered a good prognostic factor for invasive bladder cancer. This means that patients who are willing and fit enough to participate in a chemotherapy protocol tend to have a better outcome compared to those who are not eligible or unwilling to do so.

In this context, the data suggest that being able to undergo chemotherapy is an important determinant of prognosis after radical cystectomy for invasive bladder cancer. Patients who are eligible for chemotherapy tend to experience fewer complications and have a longer overall survival rate compared to those who are not eligible.

It's essential to note that single-group studies using historical or matched controls may need to be interpreted with caution, as they may not accurately represent the real-world outcomes. Additionally, prospective, randomized trials are recommended to provide more robust evidence on this topic.

In summary, eligibility for a chemotherapy protocol after radical cystectomy is considered a good prognostic factor for invasive bladder cancer, and it's essential to weigh this information against individual patient circumstances and medical needs when making treatment decisions.
